messages.subject: Bracken Group / Calderwood Industries - response to letter of claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Whitfield,

We act for Calderwood Industries Limited and refer to your letter of claim dated 5 September 2025.

Liability is denied. Our client's position, in summary, is that in or about July 2024 the parties agreed orally that an operating tolerance of 380 bar would apply to the relevant batches, which the goods met. The delivery delays are attributable in part to your client's late forecasting and to a force majeure event affecting our client's principal sub-contractor. Our client also reserves its position on quantum and on your client's failure to mitigate.

Our client is nonetheless willing to explore mediation.

Yours sincerely,
Alistair Whitlock
Partner, Pemberton Rowe LLP

messages.subject: RE: Bracken Group / Calderwood Industries - response to letter of claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Mr Whitlock,

Thank you for your letter. Our client does not accept that any variation of the pressure tolerance was agreed; in any event clause 19 of the Supply Agreement requires variations to be in writing and signed. The force majeure assertion is noted but does not appear to be supported by any contemporaneous written notice as the agreement requires.

Our client remains open to mediation but, given the time that has passed, is also preparing to issue. We will revert shortly.

Kind regards,
Sarah Whitfield

Sarah Whitfield
Partner
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
